{% comment %} One embedded cyprian editor. The textarea IS the form field — it posts, it re-renders with the submitted value after a validation error, and it is what the browser falls back to with JavaScript off. field.js hides it, mounts an editor on the host below, and writes the HTML back into it on every change. Every id derives from the widget's own id, never a literal, so several of these can sit on one page (a formset of sections, say) without fighting. {% endcomment %}
{# The toolbar and host stay empty (and the host stays out of the layout) until field.js mounts, so a JS-off page shows the textarea alone. #}
{# .cy-doc/.cy-screen carry the document typography; the editor styles its own content class inside. Height is a widget concern, not a document one. #}
{# NOT hidden here: with JavaScript off this textarea is the field, and it must be usable. field.js hides it only once an editor has mounted. #}
